questions.question: What are the basics of React Hook Form (register, handleSubmit, formState)?
questions.title: React Hook Form Basics — register, handleSubmit, formState
questions.direct_answer:
What are the basics of React Hook Form (register, handleSubmit, formState)?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** register for fields, handleSubmit wrapping onSubmit, formState.errors for validation UI, minimal re-render model via subscriptions.

**Classic weak answer:** Calling useWatch on the whole form in every render — subscribe to specific names to stay performant.

**Senior finish:** Show a typed form with register + resolver (Zod); mention useFormContext for composition.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **React Hook Form Basics — register, handleSubmit, formState** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What are the basics of React Hook Form (register, handleSubmit, formState)?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **register for fields, handleSubmit wrapping onSubmit, formState.errors for validation UI, minimal re-render model via subscriptions**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Calling useWatch on the whole form in every render — subscribe to specific names to stay performant**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Show a typed form with register + resolver (Zod); mention useFormContext for composition**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** register for fields, handleSubmit wrapping onSubmit, formState.errors for validation UI, minimal re-render model via subscriptions
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **calling useWatch on the whole form in every render — subscribe to specific names to stay performant** and what you do instead.

questions.question: How do you validate forms with React Hook Form + Zod (or Yup)?
questions.title: React Hook Form + Zod Validation — Typed Forms with Resolver
questions.direct_answer:
How do you validate forms with React Hook Form + Zod (or Yup)?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Zod schema + zodResolver passed to useForm, schema-inferred types via z.infer<typeof schema>, error messages derived from schema.

**Classic weak answer:** Duplicating validation: writing Zod schema AND TypeScript types by hand — use z.infer for single source of truth.

**Senior finish:** Recommend Zod over Yup for better TypeScript inference and modern API; show a typed form with resolver.

interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Recommend Zod over Yup for better TypeScript inference and modern API; show a typed form with resolver
